interrupted_first_512.limitation: The project saved and closed during the 40-second capture without an assistant close action. Native/Windows teardown was clean; initiating action is unknown. Excluded from matched CPU comparison.

limitations: Whole-session counters include stopped transport, save and close; they are not counts restricted to the active 40-second CPU capture. Session lengths and pre-play idle times differ.
Timing distributions cover observed correlated completions, including silence, and are not exhaustive per-note or full-session worst-case distributions; gap traces retain missed requests separately.

Current socket gaps preceded perf/capture attachment. Native detailed history retained the first gap near sequence 9927; Windows history triggered later near 10797. There are no overlapping detailed requests for cross-clock attribution in this run.

No current mailbox residual gap occurred to diagnose; historical 31.903-ms Windows reply-preparation and engine-close crash remain unexplained. The socket control also retained a distinct 31.010-ms Linux preparation interval.

Local monitor audio establishes continued output, not exact converter latency, float32 device precision or absence of device xruns. PipeWire error counters were sampled cumulatively, not as matched start/end deltas.
Short runs do not qualify 256 for long sessions; 512 remains recommended. No new 128-frame desktop claim.
The current Serum clip emitted no returned events/parameter points; return semantics are established by the production SDK fixture, not inferred from Serum audio.
Cohort CPU snapshots bracket the 40-second capture plus local sample-read/WAV-pack overhead before the second snapshot. The ~1.25% difference is not a reliable CPU-saving claim.
